content.text:
Roughly: if I put in 300 ₪ a month and take it out after 4 years, I'd get about 15,000 ₪ back. After 8 years it's about 34,000 ₪. I'm not very sure, because I never got the calculator into self-employed mode, so these are the employee numbers with the employer part set to zero.

**What decided it:** the "עצמאים" button did nothing. I tapped it three times and "שכירים" stayed chosen every time. So I put "הפקדת המעסיק" (the employer's part) at 0 and read the white bar "נשאר בידיים" (what's left in your hands).

**How it went:**
- **Top of the page:** heading "קרן השתלמות". I caught one line: after 6 years you can take the money out without tax.
- **Calculator:** I tapped the tab "מה קורה לכסף בקרן" and it jumped me to it. The switch was set to "שכירים" (employees) and "עצמאים" wouldn't switch.
- **Bar chart at 4 years:** at first it said "נשאר בידיים 52,334". I nearly took that as my answer. Then I saw "900 ₪ מהמעסיק" (900 ₪ from the employer), and I don't have one.
- **Text under the chart:** I scrolled into it: income tax, "מחיר של היום" (today's prices), 11 tracks, "חוקים וכללים". I got lost and went back up.
- **Employer at 0:** I put the employer part at 0 and left the rest as it was: 12,000 salary, 2.5%, which gives 300 ₪ a month. I didn't pick that amount, it was already there.
- **Results:** at 4 years I put in 14,400, got +1,349 and the tax took −587, so 15,162 left. At 8 years I put in 28,800, got +5,612, tax was 0, so 34,412 left.

**Words I didn't get:** "התשואה הוספה אחרי דמי ניהול" (return added after management fees), "החזר ממס הכנסה" (refund from income tax), "בכסף של היום" (in today's money), "מיטב השתלמות עוקב מדד S&P500 (13245)", "הפטור עוצר… 15,712 ₪" (the exemption stops at 15,712 ₪).

**What bothered me:**
- The self-employed button is broken, and it's exactly the part I needed.
- The first big number, 52,334, sticks in your head, and for me it's wrong.
- After 4 years you put in 14,400 and get back about 15,000. Barely anything, and there's a red striped tax piece on top.
- Grey on grey, I couldn't tell which colour is what.

If the button had worked I'd trust this more. As it is, I'd leave the page and check somewhere else whether the rules for self-employed people are different.
